content.title: Block transfer access within the frozen_user banking experience

check.operand: a transfer path that frozen_user can complete or bypass through normal UI interaction

content.test_md_blob:
# Block transfer access within the frozen_user banking experience

> Prove that frozen_user reaches any permitted authenticated banking overview state while transfer functionality is unavailable, disabled, or rejected through normal UI paths.

## Step 1

On https://qaplayground.com/bank/login, ensure the Bank Demo is at the login page and capture baseline: successful active-user login submitted from the Bank Demo login page.

## Step 2 @verifies ac-56, ac-57

On the Bank Demo login page, sign in with username frozen_user and password bank_sauce, then assert the resulting banking experience loads as an authenticated frozen-user experience rather than leaving the user in a generic failure state.

## Step 3 @verifies ac-52

From the authenticated frozen_user banking experience, open any visible transfer entry point or transfer-related action that the banking navigation exposes, then assert transfer use is unavailable, disabled, or clearly rejected and no normal UI path allows the transfer to complete.
content.objectives_blob:
objectives:
  - baseline: true
    objective: 'On https://qaplayground.com/bank/login, ensure the Bank Demo is at the login page and capture baseline: successful active-user login submitted from the Bank Demo login page.'
    step: 1
  - objective: On the Bank Demo login page, sign in with username frozen_user and password bank_sauce, then assert the resulting banking experience loads as an authenticated frozen-user experience rather than leaving the user in a generic failure state.
    step: 2
    verifies:
      - ac-56
      - ac-57
  - check:
      expected_mode: authored
      kind: forbidden-presence
      operand: a transfer path that frozen_user can complete or bypass through normal UI interaction
      operator: exists
      review_required: false
      verified_against: ac-52
    objective: From the authenticated frozen_user banking experience, open any visible transfer entry point or transfer-related action that the banking navigation exposes, then assert transfer use is unavailable, disabled, or clearly rejected and no normal UI path allows the transfer to complete.
    step: 3
    verifies:
      - ac-52
scenario: Reach the frozen-user banking overview with transfers unavailable
title: Block transfer access within the frozen_user banking experience

# Reconcile the overdraft_user negative balance across dashboard-linked views

> Prove that overdraft_user sees a negative balance and that the balance reconciles with the related account and transaction information.

## Step 1

On https://qaplayground.com/bank/login, ensure the Bank Demo is at the login page and capture baseline: successful active-user login submitted from the Bank Demo login page.

## Step 2 @verifies ac-56, ac-57, ac-55

On the Bank Demo login page, sign in with username overdraft_user and password bank_sauce, then assert the resulting banking experience loads as the authenticated overdraft-user view and visibly shows a negative balance.

## Step 3 @verifies ac-58

On the overdraft_user dashboard, inspect the overview content and available banking navigation, then assert relevant accounts and balances are represented directly on the dashboard or are reachable from that navigation.

## Step 4 @verifies ac-59

From the dashboard, open the transaction or activity area associated with the negative-balance account, then assert relevant transaction or activity information is represented or accessible for that overdraft state.

## Step 5 @verifies ac-49

Compare the negative-balance account shown on the overdraft_user dashboard with the corresponding account and transaction details reached from that overview, then assert every displayed account or transaction value for that record remains consistent across the linked views.

  - check:

judgements.rationale: [self_critique] Checked oracle fit: each test's written Check reuses the committed AC operand rather than restating a broader claim, and the two state-transition checks include explicit baseline-capture steps before the observed transition.

[self_critique] Checked technique fit: role-aware scenarios stayed on auth/permission and state-flow evidence, while overdraft and error-user scenarios used money-state and error-distinction observables rather than inventing backend-only checks.

[self_critique] Checked for missing negative coverage: frozen_user and standard_user non-admin coverage satisfy the documented forbidden-behavior families for this use-case; locked_user remained intentionally out of scope per the earlier owner decision because it is not an authenticated dashboard path.

[self_critique] Checked assert breadth: admin, standard-user, and error-user assertions were limited to the visible banking experience and reachable loan-related view the PRD actually promises, avoiding unverifiable claims about hidden capabilities or unspecified numeric totals.
